# Data Consolidate

The foundation layer. The dataset this skill produces is where every
data-dependent skill reads from by default, rather than going back to the raw
sources — and it is the only place the sources are joined and their key
mismatches classified.

**"By default" is exact, not a hedge.** Three skills also read a
raw export, and they are right to: see
`../../shared/contracts/consolidated-dataset.md`, *What this dataset is
authoritative for*. Nothing here carries a high-frequency sensor trace, and a
normalized value is not always the value as recorded.

**The reason it exists.** The majority of real manufacturing data does not arrive
through a connector. It arrives as a file. The plant already runs scheduled
exports out of its MES, historian, inspection system and planning tool, usually
into a shared drive for somebody's spreadsheet. This skill reads that folder plus
the live connectors, joins everything on the identifiers the plant already has,
and hands back one dataset with every unmatched record explained.

# Join keys and the normalization ladder

Load this before joining anything.

## Why this file exists

A plant does not have one database. It has five to eight systems bought at
different times by different departments, and the same physical thing carries a
different identifier in each one. A single part might be:

| Where | How it appears |
|---|---|
| ERP item master | `PN-4471-B` |
| MES production export | `4471B` |
| Quality inspection export | `4471-B Rev 2` |
| Maintenance spares list | `Bracket, Upper, 4471` |

All four are the same part. Only the first three are joinable, and none of them
match as-is.

## The six join keys

These are the identifiers that should be common across systems. Everything the
consolidated dataset is built around hangs off one of them.

| Join key | Links | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| Part number | Product ↔ production ↔ quality ↔ purchasing | ERP item master (NetSuite or Infor M3) |
| Production work order number | Production run ↔ output ↔ quality results ↔ cost | The ERP. In Infor M3 it is the manufacturing order number |
| Sales order number | Customer commitment ↔ production ↔ shipping | The ERP. In Infor M3 it is the customer order number |
| Lot / batch number | Material ↔ parts made from it ↔ customers who received them | MES or quality export |
| Asset ID | Machine ↔ downtime ↔ maintenance history | CMMS connector or maintenance export |
| Supplier ID / vendor number | Purchase orders ↔ incoming material ↔ supplier quality | The ERP |

**Source of truth decides direction.** When two sides disagree on a key's shape,
normalize toward the source of truth rather than toward whichever side has more
rows. The ERP item master is the reference for part numbers even when the MES
export has ten times the volume.

### The work order name collision

Maintenance systems also call their repair tickets "work orders." A production
work order and a maintenance work order are different records with different
numbering, and joining one to the other produces nonsense.

Always disambiguate in output and in column naming: **production work order** and
**maintenance work order**, never bare "work order" or "WO."

## The normalization ladder

Apply in this order. Each rung is more aggressive than the last, so stopping
early is safer than going further than needed.

| Rung | Transformation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Trim leading and trailing whitespace | Manual exports carry trailing spaces constantly |
| 2 | Normalize case | Fold to a single case for comparison only |
| 3 | Normalize punctuation | `PN-4471-B` / `PN_4471_B` / `PN4471B` collapse to one comparison form. A lost part prefix (`4471B` against `PN-4471-B`) collapses too, **only where exactly one part on the `parts` tab matches once its prefix is dropped**. Name the prefix in the log. Where two or more parts would match (`PN-4471-B` and `AX-4471-B`), nothing is matched by this rung: the record is reported with every candidate, and the plant says which |
| 4 | Restore lost leading zeros | `451` matches `00451` only if a zero-padded variant exists on the other side. Test for it; do not pad blindly |
| 5 | Strip revision suffix | `4471-B` matches `4471-B Rev 2`. The revision is extra information, not a different part |

**Rungs 1, 2 and 3 are safe to propose as automatic.** Rungs 4 and 5 change
meaning and always carry their own proposal, because a stripped revision or an
assumed zero can be wrong.

### Two hard rules

**Compare on the normalized form; store and display the original.** The
consolidated dataset carries the source system's own identifier verbatim
alongside the normalized key. A plant person searching for `PN-4471-B` in their
own vocabulary must find it. Never overwrite a source identifier with a
normalized one.

**Every normalization applied is logged and reportable.** The data quality report
names each rule that fired, how many records it touched, and an example of the
before and after. A silent normalization is indistinguishable from a bug, and the
first time a total looks wrong this log is the only way to tell them apart.

### Revision data is preserved, never discarded

When rung 5 fires, the revision that was stripped goes into its own column and
the report states that revision data existed on one side only. Stripping it to
make the join work is correct; losing it is not.

## Date windows by entity

When the user narrows the join to the overlap, the window does not apply to
every tab alike. Three kinds of record, three rules:

| Kind | Tabs | What the window does |
|---|---|---|
| **Activity** | `production_output`, `downtime_events`, `inspection_results`, `plan`, `operation_actuals` | Scoped to the overlap. A row outside it is Class 7 |
| **Open commitments** | Open `sales_orders` lines, open `production_work_orders` | **Kept by status, whatever their dates.** An open order is in scope until it closes. A sales order line that carries only a promised date and no order date is never out of window for lacking one |
| **Reference history** | `purchase_orders` and their receipts, `maintenance_work_orders`, `ncrs`, `lots` | Kept for a lookback before the window start: the Plant context's lookback if one is set, otherwise **180 days, stated as a default, not plant-set**. Labelled as history in the report and never counted in the window's totals |

Closed commitments (a shipped sales order, a closed work order) are activity:
scoped by their own close or ship date. Never class a record 7 because the
narrowing removed the history that explains it. A material receipt from

repair from June is how a breakdown is read in August.

None is a mismatch class, none is fixed silently, and each is counted in the

# What a reply holds — documents, records, memory and names

**Shared across every skill.** Four rules about what goes in front of the
person and where things are kept.

---

## Documents are printed in full; records are summarised

A **document** is what a person reads, signs or sends: the quote, the cost
sheet, the NCR, the 8D, the RFQ package, an email draft, the morning report,
the intake form. **It is printed in the reply, in full.** Saving a copy to a
file as well is fine; a file *instead of* the reply is not. The person reads
the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives in it.

### Reports are the exception: a short reply when the page was written

The morning report, the Operations page and the supplier bid comparison are
read on a page, not in the chat. For
the bid comparison the headline is the provisional recommendation and its main
tradeoff, the exceptions are the requirements still open before an award, and
the decision waiting is the next-step question. **When this run wrote the full page
somewhere the person can open** (a publish returned its URL, or the page was
saved as an HTML file and the reply names the file), the reply is a summary
of about 150 words. **200 words is a hard limit: count before sending.** Each
item below is one sentence; an exception or a decision is the thing and its
number, with the explanation left on the page.

1. Safety first, one line per item: a safety-flagged record, a record under
   *"Blocked — safety status unknown"*, or *"Safety status: not assessed"*.
2. The site, the production day, and the freshness state in one line: data
   complete, or the gap.
3. The headline: good output against plan, and OEE or why it is not computed.
4. Up to three exceptions, one line each.
5. The decisions waiting today, or *"No decisions waiting today."*
6. Where the full page is: the URL or the file path.

No tables, logs or methods in the summary; they are on the page. Every
number in the summary is one the page prints. **This is for the whole
report only.** A request that picks sections or skips some ("freshness and

"""data-consolidate run: join the pulse_oee export drop and the equipment list.

Writes one CSV per dataset tab (no XLSX writer is installed: openpyxl/xlsxwriter
absent, nothing installed), the key-mismatch log, the figures block, and the
HTML data quality report. Every figure in the report comes from this script.

import csv, os, re, html, datetime, json

ROOT = r"C:/LMFG/runs/B03-positive/work"
INP = ROOT + "/inputs"
OUT = ROOT + "/out"
DS = OUT + "/dataset"
os.makedirs(DS, exist_ok=True)
RUN = datetime.datetime.now()


def read(path):
    rows, comments = [], []
    with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        lines = f.read().splitlines()
    data = []
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if ln.startswith("#"):
            comments.append(ln)
            continue
        data.append((i, ln))
    hdr = next(csv.reader([data[0][1]]))
    for i, ln in data[1:]:
        if not ln.strip():
            continue
        vals = next(csv.reader([ln]))
        rows.append((i, dict(zip(hdr, vals))))
    return hdr, rows, comments


def mtime(path):
    return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(os.path.getmtime(path))


# ---------- Step 1: discover ----------
files = {}
for dp, _, fns in os.walk(INP):
    for fn in sorted(fns):
        files[os.path.join(dp, fn).replace("\\", "/")] = None

def fold(h):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", h.lower())

identified = []  # (file, identified_as, tab or None, note)
for p in sorted(files):
    name = os.path.basename(p)
    if not name.endswith(".csv"):
        identified.append((p, "Not a data export (readme text)", None,
                           "Read for context only: says the drop is synthetic test data."))
        continue
    hdr, rows, _ = read(p)
    h = {fold(x) for x in hdr}
    if {"assetid", "startedat", "endedat"} <= h:
        identified.append((p, "Downtime events (MES/historian export)", "downtime_events", ""))
    elif {"workorder", "qtygood", "qtyscrap"} <= h:
        identified.append((p, "Production output (MES export)", "production_output", ""))
    elif {"partnumber", "plannedqty", "plandate"} <= h:
        identified.append((p, "Plan / schedule (planning export)", "plan", ""))
    elif {"workorder", "partnumber", "qtyordered", "status"} <= h:
        identified.append((p, "Production work orders (ERP export, system not named)", "production_work_orders", ""))
    elif {"assetid", "description"} <= h:
        identified.append((p, "Asset / equipment list", "assets", ""))
    elif "opseq" in h and "workcenter" in h and "partnumber" in h:
        has_setup = any("setup" in x for x in h)
        has_run = any("run" in x for x in h)
        if has_setup and has_run:
            identified.append((p, "Routing", "routings", ""))
        else:
            identified.append((p, "UNRECOGNIZED: routing-like, missing a signature column", None,

                               "(and no revision). Per the routing signature it is not loaded and the gap is not filled."))
    else:

for p, what, tab, note in identified:
    if p.endswith(".csv"):
        src[os.path.basename(p)] = (p,) + read(p)

dt_p, _, dt_rows, _ = src["downtime.csv"]
pl_p, _, pl_rows, _ = src["plan.csv"]
wo_p, _, wo_rows, _ = src["work_orders.csv"]
rt_p, rt_h, rt_rows, _ = src["routing.csv"]

# ---------- normalization ladder (compare only) ----------
def rung1(k): return k.strip()
def rung2(k): return rung1(k).upper()
def rung3(k): return re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", rung2(k))
def rung4(k): return re.sub(r"(?<![0-9])0+(?=[0-9])", "", rung3(k))

    """Return (status, rung, partner, class)."""
    if key in universe:
        return ("matched", 0, key, None)
    for n, fn, cls in ((1, rung1, 5), (2, rung2, 5), (3, rung3, 2), (4, rung4, 3)):
        hits = [u for u in universe if fn(u) == fn(key)]
        if len(hits) == 1:
            return ("proposed_normalization", n, hits[0], cls)
    hits = [u for u in universe if rung3(rung5(u)) == rung3(rung5(key))]
    if len(hits) == 1:
        return ("proposed_normalization", 5, hits[0], 4)
    return ("unmatched", None, None, 1)

asset_master = [r["asset_id"] for _, r in eq_rows]
wo_master = [r["work_order"] for _, r in wo_rows]
wo_part = {r["work_order"]: r["part_number"] for _, r in wo_rows}
parts_seen_wo = sorted(set(wo_part.values()))

mismatch_log = []  # dicts

    status, rung, partner, cls = res
    mismatch_log.append(dict(tab=tab, source_ref=f"{rel(srcfile)}:{line}", key=key_type,

                             ladder_rung=rung if rung is not None else "",
                             partner=partner or "", mismatch_class=cls or "",
                             note=note))

          "mismatch_class", "contradicted_by", "integrity_flags"]

    """Row-level join_status: worst of its keys."""

        return "unmatched", cls[0]

    return "matched", None

# activity window

             "downtime.csv": sorted({r["started_at"][:10] for _, r in dt_rows} | {r["ended_at"][:10] for _, r in dt_rows}),
             "plan.csv": sorted({r["plan_date"] for _, r in pl_rows})}
win = {k: (v[0], v[-1]) for k, v in act_dates.items()}
ov_start = max(v[0] for v in win.values()); ov_end = min(v[1] for v in win.values())
overlap_ok = ov_start <= ov_end

def future(ts):
    try:
        d = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(ts) if "T" in ts else datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(ts + "T00:00:00")
    except ValueError:

    return d > RUN

SITE_UNSTATED = "not stated in source"

# ---------- assets ----------
used_assets = {}
for f, rows in (("output.csv", out_rows), ("downtime.csv", dt_rows), ("plan.csv", pl_rows)):
    for _, r in rows:

assets_tab = []
for ln, r in eq_rows:
    a = r["asset_id"]
    used = a in {rung2(x) for x in used_assets} or any(match(x, [a])[0] != "unmatched" for x in used_assets)
    assets_tab.append(dict(site=SITE_UNSTATED, source_system="manual",

                           as_of=f"{mtime(eq_p).date()} (file modified date; source records no date, zone unresolved)",
                           join_status="matched" if used else "unmatched",
                           mismatch_class="" if used else 6, contradicted_by="", integrity_flags="",
                           asset_id=rung1(a), asset_id_verbatim=a, location=r["cell"]))
    if not used:
        log("assets", eq_p, ln, "asset", a, ("unmatched", None, None, 6),
            "On the equipment list; appears in no output, downtime or plan row. No other source records activity on it.")

# ---------- production_work_orders ----------
out_wos = {r["work_order"] for _, r in out_rows}
pwo_tab = []
for ln, r in wo_rows:
    has_out = r["work_order"] in out_wos
    pwo_tab.append(dict(site=SITE_UNSTATED, source_system="manual", source_ref=f"{rel(wo_p)}:{ln}",
                        as_of=f"{mtime(wo_p).date()} (file modified date; source records no date, zone unresolved)",
                        join_status="matched" if has_out else "unmatched",
                        mismatch_class="" if has_out else 6, contradicted_by="", integrity_flags="",
                        production_wo=rung1(r["work_order"]), production_wo_verbatim=r["work_order"],
                        part_number=rung1(r["part_number"]), part_number_verbatim=r["part_number"],
                        qty=r["qty_ordered"], uom="", due_date=r["due_date"], status=r["status"],
                        sales_order="", sales_order_verbatim=""))

# ---------- production_output ----------
po_tab = []
grain = {}
for ln, r in out_rows:
    rw = match(r["work_order"], wo_master); log("production_output", out_p, ln, "production work order", r["work_order"], rw)
    rp_res = ("matched", 0, r["part_number"], None) if wo_part.get(r["work_order"]) == r["part_number"] else ("unmatched", None, None, 1)
    log("production_output", out_p, ln, "part (vs work order's part)", r["part_number"], rp_res)
    ra = match(r["asset_id"], asset_master)
    log("production_output", out_p, ln, "asset", r["asset_id"], ra,
        "" if ra[0] == "matched" else "Asset ID not on the equipment list under any ladder rung.")
    st, cls = row_status([rw, rp_res, ra])
    win_ok = ov_start <= r["production_day"] <= ov_end
    if not win_ok:
        st, cls = "unmatched", 7
    flags = ["future_timestamp"] if future(r["production_day"]) else []
    g = (r["work_order"], r["shift"], r["production_day"]); grain.setdefault(g, []).append(ln)
    po_tab.append(dict(site=r["site"], source_system="mes_export", source_ref=f"{rel(out_p)}:{ln}",
                       as_of=f"{r['production_day']} (date only; zone unresolved)",
                       join_status=st, mismatch_class=cls or "", contradicted_by="",
